top_signals.title: Crypto industry reels as April sees highest number of hacks ever
top_signals.summary: April recorded a historic 29 crypto hacks, the highest monthly total ever, resulting in a combined loss of $579 million from the Drift exchange and Kelp DAO. The majority of incidents were caused by code bugs and single points of failure, highlighting growing security concerns in DeFi.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The surge to 29 hacks and $579 million losses underscores heightened security risk, likely compressing DeFi valuations and prompting VCs to prioritize funding for audit, insurance and formal‑verification infrastructure.

top_signals.title: DeFi absorbs $292 million shock as AAVE-led rescue steadies markets: Standard Chartered
top_signals.summary: A $292 million exploit on KelpDAO cascaded into AAVE, triggering a sharp liquidity crunch in DeFi. An AAVE‑led $300 million rescue, backed by a coalition of DeFi firms, helped stabilise deposits and yields, reinforcing the sector’s resilience and supporting a $2 trillion tokenised RWA outlook by 2028.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Aave’s $300 million rescue shows that coordinated liquidity backstops can stabilize DeFi after large exploits, reinforcing Aave’s market position and supporting the $2 trillion tokenised RWA thesis that may attract new institutional capital.

top_signals.title: Aave-led 'DeFi United' campaign raises $300m to address Kelp DAO breach
top_signals.summary: Aave has spearheaded the DeFi United campaign, raising over $300 million to reimburse victims of the Kelp DAO/LayerZero hack that stole $293 million. Major DAOs, crypto businesses and notable figures have pledged large sums of Ether and stablecoins to the recovery fund, signaling strong community solidarity despite some controversy.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $300 million DeFi United fund demonstrates strong community capital mobilisation, suggesting that future breach mitigation may rely on pooled rescue mechanisms rather than individual protocol balance sheets.

top_signals.title: Ethereum Backers Commit 30,000 ETH to rsETH Recovery After Exploit
top_signals.summary: An April 18 exploit drained roughly 116,500 rsETH ($290 M) from a LayerZero‑based bridge run by Kelp DAO, causing up to $200 M of bad debt on Aave. In response, a coalition of DeFi projects (DeFi United) backed by Lido, EtherFi, Ethena, Mantle, Frax and others pledged 30,000 ETH to aid recovery, while Circle’s venture arm bought AAVE tokens to support the ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The pledge of 30,000 ETH by major Ethereum stakeholders signals that core infrastructure players are willing to inject native assets to protect bridge liquidity, which could set a precedent for on‑chain risk‑sharing arrangements.

top_signals.title: Vitalik-backed MegaETH sees token fall 55% on first day trading
top_signals.summary: MegaETH, an Ethereum layer‑2 network backed by Vitalik Buterin, launched its MEGA token which dropped 55% on its first day of trading, falling to about $0.17. The project has raised roughly $108 million across token sales, a $10 million Echo round, venture funding and NFT sales, but its on‑chain activity remains modest.
top_signals.why_it_matters: MegaETH’s 55 percent price collapse highlights the volatility of layer‑2 token launches and suggests that venture capital may become more cautious about funding token‑centric roll‑outs without proven usage metrics.

top_signals.title: Is Aave too Big to Fail?
top_signals.summary: A recent rsETH exploit caused a $193 M loss on Aave, but the ecosystem rallied with DeFi United contributing over $300 M to fully reimburse depositors. Despite a 45 % TVL drawdown, Aave still commands roughly half of the top‑six lending market and is viewed as undervalued with future catalysts unpriced.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Aave’s ability to weather a $193 million loss and retain ~50 percent of lending market share reinforces its “too‑big‑to‑fail” perception, potentially justifying higher valuations and attracting capital seeking exposure to a de‑facto core protocol.

worth_a_read.note: Record‑high DeFi hack wave underscores security fragility April saw 29 crypto hacks , the most ever recorded in a single month , wiping out $579 million, with the Drift exchange and Kelp DAO among the biggest victims. The incidents were largely traced to code bugs and single points of failure, highlighting that even mature DeFi protocols remain vulnerable. Blockwall should anticipate heightened demand for formal security audits, bug‑bounty platforms and insurance products that can protect DeFi infrastructure investors.

Aave‑driven “DeFi United” rescue proves systemic clout and community solidarity Following the Kelp DAO exploit, Aave coordinated a $300 million rescue fund that attracted pledges from multiple DAOs, crypto firms and high‑profile individuals. The coalition also contributed 30,000 ETH to plug a $246 million hole left by the attack, reinforcing Aave’s role as a de‑facto backstop for the lending market. This pattern suggests that large‑scale, protocol‑level safety nets may become a standard expectation for investors in DeFi infrastructure.

Non‑USD stablecoins gain regulatory approval and user adoption Israel’s Capital Market Authority approved the first regulated shekel‑pegged stablecoin (BILS) issued on Solana with custodianship by Fireblocks and audit by EY, marking a clear move away from USD‑centric stablecoins. At the same time, Bitso’s 2025 adoption report showed stablecoins capturing 40 % of crypto purchases in Latin America, overtaking Bitcoin’s 18 % share. The twin developments point to a diversification of stablecoin rails that could open new tokenisation opportunities and reduce reliance on US‑dollar pegs.

Institutional Bitcoin accumulation and geopolitical positioning reinforce long‑term confidence Strategy (MSTR) added $255 million of Bitcoin, bringing its treasury to 818,334 BTC valued at roughly $61.8 billion, while the U.S. Pentagon publicly confirmed classified Bitcoin projects, framing the asset as a national‑security tool. Despite short‑term price dips below $75 k after the Fed’s rate decision, these actions signal sustained institutional belief in Bitcoin as a store of value and strategic asset, supporting continued capital inflows into Bitcoin‑related infrastructure.

Stablecoin‑enabled payments bridge traditional finance and Web3 ecosystems Meta launched creator payouts in Circle’s USDC on Polygon and Solana via Stripe, initially targeting Colombia and the Philippines, and Shinhan Card announced a partnership with Solana to offer stablecoin‑based card payments and DeFi services in Korea. OKX’s open‑standard payment protocol for autonomous AI agents further expands the use‑case spectrum. The convergence of stablecoins, payment processors and legacy finance institutions suggests a rapid scaling of wallet/identity solutions that can capture cross‑border transaction volume.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, April 21‑27 was a turbulent week for crypto, underscoring both the fragility and the resilience of the ecosystem. The headline was a record‑high 29 hacks in a single month, wiping out $579 million from the Drift exchange and Kelp DAO. Most of the breaches traced back to code bugs and single points of failure, sending a clear signal that security hygiene must become a board‑level priority for every DeFi protocol. The fallout triggered a cascade that tested the depth of the market. A $292 million exploit on Kelp DAO spilled over into Aave, creating a sharp liquidity crunch across DeFi. In response, Aave led a “DeFi United” rescue effort that raised more than $300 million from a coalition of DAOs, crypto businesses and prominent individuals. The fund aims to reimburse victims and shore up the breached bridge, while Circle’s venture arm allocated AAVE tokens to reinforce the broader ecosystem. This coordinated response demonstrates that, despite controversy, the community can mobilise quickly when capital is at risk. Parallel to the crisis, Ethereum’s core supporters pledged 30,000 ETH to aid the rsETH recovery effort. Projects such as Lido, EtherFi, Ethena, Mantle and Frax joined forces, illustrating a growing trend of cross‑project risk mitigation. Meanwhile, Vitalik‑backed MegaETH launched its MEGA token, only to see a 55 % drop on day one, highlighting that even well‑funded layer‑2 ventures face market discipline. On the macro side, stablecoin supply nudged up 1.2 % to $260 billion, Bitcoin spot ETFs attracted $500 million in net inflows, and DeFi total value locked slipped 0.8 % to $118 billion. Ethereum daily active addresses rose 3.5 % to 1.48 million, suggesting user interest remains robust despite short‑term shocks. The week reinforces two takeaways for European investors: security must be baked into every token design, and collaborative capital pools can act as a first line of defence against systemic risk. As we look ahead, what emerging protocols do you see best positioned to turn these lessons into lasting value? #Web3 #Crypto #Blockchain #CryptoVC #WeeklyDigest
